title: Compare databases - SchemaScope v3 walkthrough
voice: Kokoro am_michael, about 2.2-2.4 words/s, no lone one-word lines
style: White / light theme throughout. Character only in scene 1. Yellow highlight bar only in scene 1 (hook) and scene 13 (close). Scenes 4-12 copy the v1 walkthrough: one steady real app frame per step, a numbered blue step pill (1-8) with one short caption at the bottom, one slow camera move per step, a cursor doing the work. No big headlines over the app.
reuse: All app frames are v2 shots (assets/video/v2/shots, 2x, boxes in 1920x1080 CSS px from manifest.json). Character: assets/video/v2/character/character.svg (scene 1 only). Engine to copy (not modify): v2/scene.html renderAt(t), render.mjs, voice.py, sound.py. v1 caption pill style: assets/video/scene.html #cap/#capnum/#captext, restyled for light theme.
redactions: Runs as 'Windows: DESKTOP-...\Admin' on the apply dialog (29/30/31) and the Protected dialog (37): grey redaction chip 'Windows: (hidden)', exactly as in v2
Output folder path 'C:\Users\Admin\...' on 26-* and 28-scripts-written: redaction chip, as in v2
Any LAN IP or local folder path that appears anywhere else: redaction chip (none expected in the frames chosen; keep the v2 rule)

scenes.name: Compare databases
scenes.visual: White canvas, faint 40px grid. 'Compare databases.' lands on the yellow highlight bar, heavy near-black type, centre-left. Under it three small grey pills type on with the voice: 'Staging' - 'Production' - 'Every client database'. The last pill fans into eight tiny database icons (Client01-08). The developer character (v2/character/character.svg, neutral, friendly) pops up bottom-right and points at the pills. This is the ONLY appearance of the character in the whole video; he slides out at 4.0-4.4 s and never comes back. Tag bottom-left in small grey: 'illustration'.
scenes.caption: [Compare databases.]  Staging - Production - Every client database
scenes.voiceover: Compare databases. Staging, production, and every client database.
scenes.sound: One soft bass hit as the yellow bar wipes in; three light ticks for the three pills; calm music bed starts under it.

scenes.name: One database, many clients - who has what?
scenes.visual: Same white grid, no character, no yellow. One blue source database card in the middle-left ('SSDemo_Dev', name on screen only). Thin lines draw out to eight client cards on the right (Client01-08). As the voice says each phrase, a small grey question tag appears on the client cards: 'which tables?', then 'which procedure is missing?', then 'which schema never shipped?'. On the last one, Client04's card shows an empty 'support' folder outline. Slow push-in, no other motion. Small grey tag: 'illustration'.
scenes.caption: which tables?  -  which procedure is missing?  -  which schema never shipped?
scenes.voiceover: We ship one database to many clients. Soon nobody knows which client has which tables, which procedure is missing, or which schema never shipped.
scenes.sound: Music bed only, low and calm; a soft paper tick per question tag.

scenes.name: The easy fix
scenes.visual: The illustration cross-fades into the real app, empty compare screen (01-empty-compare.png), Write mode switch visibly Off. Camera starts slightly pushed in on the header with the SchemaScope logo, then eases out to the full window. Small grey line under the window: 'Real app, demo data'. No pill yet.
scenes.caption: SchemaScope - real app, demo data
scenes.voiceover: The easy fix: compare them with SchemaScope.
scenes.sound: A gentle rising swell into the cross-fade, then music continues.

scenes.name: Pick the source you trust
scenes.visual: Cursor clicks the Source slot (box 67,58 224x33) on 01-empty-compare; the real picker opens (02-picker-source: filtered 'SSDemo', SSDemo_Dev row selected). Cursor clicks 'Use this database' (1144,814); cut to 03-source-picked with SSDemo_Dev in the source slot. Camera: one slow push-in toward the dialog, then settles on the source slot. Step pill 1.
scenes.caption: 1  Pick the source you trust
scenes.voiceover: First, pick the database you trust.
scenes.sound: Soft tick as pill 1 appears; mouse click on 'Use this database'.

scenes.name: Add every target
scenes.visual: Steady app frame. Cursor clicks 'Add target' (04-picker-target, SSDemo_QA selected), then the chips fill in one by one: 05-targets-01 .. 05-targets-09 (about 0.3 s each: QA, Client01 ... Client08), ending on 06-setup-ready with all nine chips. Camera: one slow pan left to right along the chip row (target-chips box 534,65 1349x33).
scenes.caption: 2  Add every target - QA + 8 clients
scenes.voiceover: Add every target: Q A and eight clients.
scenes.sound: A light pop per chip (nine pops), quiet.

scenes.name: Compare - all at once
scenes.visual: 07-compare-hover: cursor on Compare (116,115 96x31), click. 09-comparing-warm: the progress strip shows all ten databases 'Reading catalog' at the same time (hold ~1 s, the real warm run length). Cut to 10-results-dashboard. Camera: slow pull-out from the button to the progress strip to the whole window. Small grey note under the caption: '9 targets in 890-985 ms warm (5 runs) - first run after app start 2.8 s - LocalDB, demo data'. The app's own '1130 ms' (UI round-trip) stays visible and is not hidden.
scenes.caption: 3  Compare - all 9 at once, about a second
scenes.voiceover: Press Compare. All nine at once, in about a second.
scenes.sound: Click on Compare, a short soft whoosh while the bars run, a clean chime when the dashboard lands.

scenes.name: A score for every client, worst first
scenes.visual: 10-results-dashboard: camera pushes gently onto the tile row (dashboard box 0,158 1920x244) starting at Client03 88.8% and Client04 88.9%, then cross-dissolves to 11-results-dashboard-scrolled while panning right to the healthy end (Client06 98.9, Client01 99.2, QA 99.8). One thin blue underline sweeps under the scores left to right; nothing else added.
scenes.caption: 4  A score for every client - worst first
scenes.voiceover: Every client gets a score, worst first.
scenes.sound: Nine very soft ticks as the underline passes each score.

scenes.name: Find what is missing
scenes.visual: Part A (33.4-37.4): 14-matrix-grid-tall (all 9 targets, differences only, 454 of 1,241). Camera pushes into the first row 'Schema support.support' and the red X under SSDEMO_CLIENT04 (row y~277, column x~1326 CSS px); a thin red ring draws round that X. Small label next to it: 'Client04: 127 missing - the whole support schema never deployed'. Part B (37.4-41.2): camera slides left to the SSDEMO_CLIENT03 column (x~1194) and its red X marks: billing.BillingCycle (y~512) and hr.Department (y~850) - missing tables. Label: 'Client03: 58 missing'. If shot 46 (needed_new_shots) is captured, Part B instead uses it to show Client03's missing tables AND procedures in one filtered list; if not, the voiceover line for Client03 becomes 'Client three is missing tables.'
scenes.caption: 5  Find what is missing
scenes.voiceover: See what is missing. Client four never got the support schema. Client three lacks tables and procedures.
scenes.sound: A soft low tone as the red ring draws; nothing else.

scenes.name: Open any object side by side
scenes.visual: 15-diff-changed-proc: core.usp_Currency_List, SSDemo_Dev on the left vs SSDemo_Client03 on the right. Cursor clicks the grid row (0,266), the diff opens. Camera: one slow push-in onto the changed line on the right, 'AND t.Status <> 9' (box 990,785 900x16), with a pale yellow wash on that single line only (not a headline bar). Status badge 'Different +1 -0' stays visible top-right.
scenes.caption: 6  Open any object side by side - see the exact lines
scenes.voiceover: Open any object to see the exact lines.
scenes.sound: Click; a soft page turn as the diff opens.

scenes.name: Create the fix scripts
scenes.visual: 20-hero-tile-create-scripts-hover: cursor on the 'Create scripts' icon of the SSDemo_Client05 tile (97.7%). Click: 21-create-scripts-dialog-readonly (numbered folders). Cut to 28-scripts-written: real folder list (01_columns 4, 03_missing 13, 04_columntypes 4, 05_constraints 6, 06_indexes 7) and the green line 'Checked offline: 173 batches parse, and 24 of 24 code bodies match the source exactly.' Camera: slow push-in onto the green line. The 'Written to' path is covered by the redaction chip. Write mode is still Off in 20/21 (28 was captured with Write mode On; the amber strip is visible - acceptable, it leads into step 8).
scenes.caption: 7  Create the fix scripts - checked offline
scenes.voiceover: Create the fix scripts, checked offline first.
scenes.sound: Click; a light paper swish as the folder list appears; a small chime on the green line.

scenes.name: Write mode (new in 1.2) - type the name to apply
scenes.visual: Small 'NEW IN 1.2' tag above pill 8 (tag, not a headline). 22-write-mode-switch-off: camera eases to the header switch 'Write mode Off'. Cursor clicks: 23b-write-mode-confirm-hover ('Turn on write mode?' dialog, cursor on 'Enable for this session'). Click: 24-write-mode-on (switch amber, amber strip). Cut to the apply dialog 29-apply-dialog, then the confirm box types the name: 30-apply-typing-03 / 07 / 11 / 13, ending on 31-apply-name-typed with 'Apply 34 files to SSDemo_Client05' enabled. 'Runs as' covered by the redaction chip. Camera: one slow move from the header switch down to the confirm box.
scenes.caption: 8  Write mode - turn it on, type the name, apply
scenes.voiceover: New in one point two: write mode. Type the name to apply.
scenes.sound: A solid latch click when the switch turns amber; soft key clicks per letter.

scenes.name: Client05 at 100% - Protected servers refused
scenes.visual: Pill 8 stays. Cursor clicks Apply. 34-apply-result: 'Applied all 34 file(s) to SSDemo_Client05.' and the line 'Compared again: SSDemo_Client05 now matches the source 100%'. Cut to 35-recompared-hero-100: camera settles on the SSDemo_Client05 tile at 100.0% (box 1310,241). Small grey label: 'was 97.7% in the 9-target compare'. Then (57.6-59.6) a clean cut to 37-protected-apply-refused: Apply to SSDemo_Client08 on a Protected connection - red banner 'Protected server - scripts only.', no confirm box, only Close. Camera pushes gently onto the red banner. 'Runs as' covered by the redaction chip.
scenes.caption: 8  Client05: 97.7% -> 100%  -  Protected servers: refused
scenes.voiceover: Client five goes to one hundred percent. Protected servers are refused.
scenes.sound: Click on Apply, a quick run of tiny ticks, a warm resolve chord at 100%; a dull soft thud on the Protected banner.

scenes.name: Stop comparing in pairs
scenes.visual: Cross-fade to the white grid. SchemaScope logo centred. 'Stop comparing in pairs.' lands on the yellow highlight bar (second and last use of the bar). Under it a quiet row of pills: Free - Open source - SQL Server 2012+ - Azure SQL - Windows 10 & 11. Button: 'Free download - schemascope.shadowmark.in'. No character.
scenes.caption: [Stop comparing in pairs.]  Free download - schemascope.shadowmark.in
scenes.voiceover: Stop comparing in pairs. Free at schema scope dot shadow mark dot in.
scenes.sound: Music swells gently and resolves; one soft hit as the yellow bar lands.

needed_new_shots.name: 45-matrix-missing-client04.png (optional)
needed_new_shots.ui_state: Same 9-target compare as 10-results-dashboard (light theme, 1920x1080 at 2x, Write mode Off). Dashboard collapsed as in 14-matrix-grid-tall. Status filter = Missing only, target dropdown = 'Only SSDemo_Client04', Differences only ticked. Grid lists Schema support.support and the support.* objects (Ticket, TicketComment, Sla, SupportQueue, ...) each with the red X under SSDEMO_CLIENT04. Record the row count the toolbar shows and add element boxes for the support.support row and the CLIENT04 column header to manifest.
needed_new_shots.why: Makes step 5 'Client04 never got the support schema' unmistakable: a whole list of support objects missing, not just one row. 14-matrix-grid-tall already shows the support.support X, so this is an upgrade, not a blocker.

needed_new_shots.name: 46-matrix-missing-client03.png (needed for the Client03 'procedures' claim)
needed_new_shots.ui_state: Same compare, dashboard collapsed. Status filter = Missing only, target dropdown = 'Only SSDemo_Client03'. Grid scrolled so both missing Tables (billing.BillingCycle, hr.Department, ...) and missing Procedures (type column 'Procedure') are visible with red X under SSDEMO_CLIENT03. Add boxes for one missing table row and one missing procedure row.
needed_new_shots.why: No existing frame shows a missing procedure for Client03 (14 only shows missing tables; 13 is filtered to Different, not Missing). Without this shot, change the step 5 voiceover to 'Client three is missing tables.' to stay honest.

hook_loop: 6 s silent loop, no voiceover, no character: white grid; 'Compare databases.' lands on the yellow bar; the real 10-results-dashboard tile row slides up under it with all nine scores (88.8 ... 99.8) landing in the same frame; one blue sweep crosses the row; fade back to the empty grid for a seamless loop.
honesty_notes: All scores, counts and timings come from v2/demo-db/measurements.json and the v2 screenshots.
Compare time: 890-985 ms warm over 5 runs, 2.8 s for the first run after app start. Both are on screen in step 3. The app's own 1130 ms UI round-trip is left visible.
Client04: 127 missing, the support schema was never created (build.py DRIFT missing_schemas=('support',)).
Client03: 58 missing (3 tables + 55 modules). The word 'procedures' is spoken only if shot 46 shows a missing procedure; otherwise the line is 'Client three is missing tables.'
Client05: 97.7% in the 9-target compare; after applying 34 files the re-compare reports 100%. The tile label says which compare each figure comes from.
Client08 was marked Protected for the demo; the apply panel refuses it.
Staging and production in the hook and the story are illustrations; the demo databases are QA and Client01-08 on LocalDB, labelled 'demo data'.
tts_rules: Never speak 'Dev' (heard as 'death') - shown on screen only
Numbers as words; 'Client04' spoken 'Client four', 'Client05' 'Client five'
URL spoken 'schema scope dot shadow mark dot in'
